Of the sources here, only the Irish Times piece comes even close to the expectation for reliable/independent sourcing (the gallerypress.com webpage is connected to one of the winners; the rest are the issuing org's own website). If there are no other/independent sources, then notability doesn't seem to be established. Does this award even need its own standalone title? Could it not be readily covered WP:WITHIN the article on the org that awards the prize? (Same goes for :Draft:Southword Debut Poetry Collection Award (on another prize issued by the same org and created by the same contributor). Guliolopez (talk) 15:37, 16 February 2026 (UTC)}}
----
The Farmgate Café National Poetry Award is a poetry award for the best original collection of poetry in a calendar year by a poet living in Ireland. It is awarded by the Munster Literature Centre, and is sponsored by the Farmgate Café in the English Market, Cork. The award offers a prize of €2,000. It was first offered in 2019, and was won by Leanne O'Sullivan. Since 2023, the highest scoring debut collection on the shortlist that does not win has been awarded the Southword Debut Poetry Collection Award, worth €1,000.
